comparison: Both evaluate eCLIP data identifying RBP interactions with ASAR6-141 (C4, C5, C50, C51) and clustering in the ~7kb region (C6, C52, C53). OpenEval addresses these as two separate result groups (R1 and R2), while peer review combines them. Both find the data convincing and supported, with peer reviewers describing images as 'impressive.'

OpenEval R2 focuses specifically on RBP binding site clustering in the ~7kb domain (C6, C52, C53, C90). Peer R1 includes these claims alongside the broader RBP identification findings. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with similar positive assessments of the data quality.

Perfect alignment on claims C7, C54-C58 regarding CRISPR deletion of ~7kb RBPD causing delayed replication. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and describe the data as convincing, with peer reviewers noting this 'expands upon our understanding on the role of hnRNP proteins in lncRNA function.'

Strong overlap on transgene integration experiments (C60-C65). OpenEval also includes claims about effects on inactive X (C76, C77) that peer R3 addresses. Both are SUPPORTED, though OpenEval notes variable transgene expression as a caveat while peer reviewer questions whether integration into active X was tested.

Both evaluate RBP depletion causing ASAR dissociation from chromosome territory (C8-C13, C66-C68). Peer R4 also includes broader claims about ASAR dissociation (C78, C80). Both are SUPPORTED with descriptions of 'convincing' FISH data and 'impressive' image quality.

Perfect alignment on negative control experiments (C69, C81) showing specificity of RBP effects. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval explicitly discusses how these controls strengthen conclusions about specific RBP-ASAR interactions, while peer reviewers accept without challenge.

Both address XIST RNA dissociation following RBP depletion (C70-C73). OpenEval is SUPPORTED but notes interpretation of 'dissociation' is somewhat speculative. Peer review is SUPPORTED and describes findings as 'compelling results suggesting shared mechanism(s)' between ASARs and Xist regulation.

Both evaluate transgene effects on inactive X (C74, C75, C111, C112). OpenEval is SUPPORTED but notes mechanistic interpretation of 'interference' (C113) is speculative. Peer review is UNCERTAIN, questioning whether integration into active X was tested and whether altered Xist expression might confound interpretation.

Partial overlap on transgene integration causing DRT/DMC (C76, C77). OpenEval R8 focuses on X chromosome effects while peer R3 addresses both autosome and X chromosome integration. Both are SUPPORTED regarding the basic findings.

Partial overlap on ASAR dissociation claims (C78, C80). OpenEval R9 specifically addresses multiple ASAR RNAs and their colocalization in cytoplasmic foci following RBP depletion. Peer R4 addresses ASAR6-141 dissociation more broadly. Both are SUPPORTED.

Strong overlap on genome-wide asynchronous replication following RBP depletion (C14, C82-C84, C92). Peer R5 also includes C15 and C100. Both are SUPPORTED and describe results as 'compelling' or 'convincing,' with agreement on the statistical significance and genome-wide nature of the effect.

Partial overlap on DRT/DMC phenotype frequency (C85, C86). OpenEval R11 is SUPPORTED but notes quantification appears based on visual assessment rather than systematic analysis. Peer R5 describes overall results as 'compelling' without specifically critiquing quantification methods.

Partial overlap on comparison between RBP depletion and ASAR knockout phenotypes (C15, C100). OpenEval R12 is SUPPORTED, noting consistency provides strong evidence for functional relationship. Peer R5 is SUPPORTED and describes results as 'compelling.'

Minimal overlap on claim C100 regarding phenotype comparison. OpenEval R12 is SUPPORTED regarding the functional relationship evidence. Peer R8 is UNCERTAIN about mechanistic interpretation, cautioning against 'over interpretation that hnRNP proteins can regulate chromosome replication directly.'

Perfect alignment on C0T-1 RNA and ASAR connection (C38, C39, C87). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes some uncertainty about extent of C0T-1 RNA representing ASARs vs. other repeat-rich RNAs. Peer reviewers accept findings without explicit critique.

Strong overlap on mechanistic model claims (C16, C93, C94). Both evaluations are UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the 'RNA scaffold' mechanism requires additional biochemical evidence. Peer reviewers caution about 'over interpretation,' noting 'mechanism is not much clearer than before' and effects 'may be indirect.'

Both address mechanistic interpretation of ASAR displacement causing replication defects (C103). Both are UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes causal relationship and specific mechanism remain speculative. Peer reviewers state 'exact effects of knockdown experiments are unclear and may be indirect.'

Minimal overlap on claim C113 regarding interference mechanism on inactive X. OpenEval R15 is UNCERTAIN about mechanistic interpretation. Peer R7 is UNCERTAIN, questioning whether effects might be confounded by altered Xist expression rather than direct interference.

Perfect alignment on background claims about ASAR characteristics (C1-C3, C18-C26, C88-C89). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are well-documented across multiple publications. Peer reviewers accept without challenge and describe ASARs as 'relatively novel genes...of broad significance.'

OpenEval R17 addresses background claims about ASAR6 RNA requirement for replication timing (C27-C31, C37, C102) supported by prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though these background claims are not contested.

OpenEval R18 addresses allele-specific requirement of ASAR function (C59) supported by current and prior experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though allele-specificity is acknowledged in peer R2.

OpenEval R19 provides integrative assessment of RBP-ASAR interactions (C96-C99) across multiple experimental approaches. Evaluation is SUPPORTED. No corresponding discrete peer review result, though individual experiments are evaluated positively in peer R1-R5.

OpenEval R20 addresses condensate model claims (C104-C109) combining literature citations with experimental observations. Evaluation is SUPPORTED though notes direct evidence for ASAR-containing condensates not provided. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R21 addresses comparison with Xist deletion phenotypes (C114-C116) based on literature. Evaluation is SUPPORTED but notes 'shared mechanism' is speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation, though peer R6 mentions 'shared mechanism(s)' positively.

OpenEval R22 addresses various background claims (C17, C32-C36, C40-C46, C110) supported by literature. Evaluation is SUPPORTED. No corresponding discrete peer review result, though background context is not contested by reviewers.

OpenEval R23 addresses variability in RNA-FISH signal (C47-C49). Evaluation is SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about potential sources of variability. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R24 addresses estimate of ASAR coverage in genome (C95) based on prior work. Evaluation is SUPPORTED but notes independent validation would be valuable. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
